title: Rabbah son of Rav Yitzchak
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman notes that we always find Rabbah son of Rav Yitzchak transmitting in Rav’s name, as in [Yevamot 71b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.71b.14), [Bava Batra 77a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.77a.2) and [Chullin 45b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.45b.6); and in [Kiddushin 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.27a.2) and [Sanhedrin 98b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.98b.10) and 99b he quotes the name Rava son of Rav Yitzchak in the same formula.

Afterward he sat before Rav Yehudah, as in [Avodah Zarah 55a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.55a.8): “Rava son of Rav Yitzchak said to Rav Yehudah.” In [Menachot 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.26b.11): “Rav Yehudah said to Rabbah son of Rav Yitzchak: I will explain it to you.”

We find in [Sotah 46b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.46b.14): “Ravina accompanied Rava bar Yitzchak four cubits in the city; danger came upon him and he was saved.” Hyman considers this a scribal error and reports finding his preferred reading in the Tosafot on the Torah, end of parashah Shoftim, where he reads “Ravina accompanied Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak.” Hyman says that Seder HaDorot did not notice the scribal error.[^3]

notes.text: All always assertions, proposed Rav/Rava and Nachman substitutions, and Soncino/Tosafot-on-Torah reading reports remain Hyman’s. The supplied Menachot26a locator is retained without claiming a new primary match.

The consulted Chullin 45b directly has Rabbah bar Yitzchak reporting Rav. This does not establish every occurrence, the later Rav Yehudah chronology or Hyman’s preferred Nachman reading of Sotah. The always assertion, Tosafot-on-Torah reading and Seder HaDorot criticism retain Hyman’s force and attribution; exact editions remain uninspected.

Bava Batra has Rabbah and Kiddushin has Rava for a corresponding transmission in Rav’s name. Menachot 26b names Rabbah son of Rav Yitzchak as Rav Yehudah’s addressee. Sotah reads Rava bar Yitzchak, beside Hyman’s preferred Nachman.
